raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`benchmark/hicache/bench_warm_cache.py` can silently under-report **output token throughput** under high concurrency / long streaming requests: some requests finish with HTTP 200 but are recorded as `success` with `output_len == 0`, so `Total generated tokens` ends up an exact multiple of `output_len` short of `completed * output_len` and `output_throughput` is deflated — even though the server actually generated the tokens (engine `gen throughput` logs confirm generation). This is a **benchmark-only** measurement bug; no serving/runtime code is involved.

Root cause in `async_request_sglang_generate`:
1. The token count is only updated inside `if "text" in data and data["text"]:`. A request whose chunks never hit that branch (chunk-boundary / cumulative-text handling under load) keeps `output_len == 0` and never reads `meta_info.completion_tokens`.
2. Any HTTP 200 is marked `output.success = True` regardless of whether tokens were received, so 0-token streams are silently counted into the denominator.

Observed on a 32K-input / 1K-output / 75%-shared-prefix run: at concurrency 10, ~1/3 of runs reported e.g. `Successful requests: 30` but `Total generated tokens: 27648` (= 27×1024) — a few "successful" requests contributed 0 tokens.

## Modifications

- Read `meta_info.completion_tokens` on **any** chunk that carries it (monotonic max), decoupled from whether `text` is non-empty; keep TTFT on the first counted token and distribute ITL over new tokens.
- If a 200 response yielded **0** counted tokens, mark it `success = False` with an explicit error so it surfaces in the `WARNING x/y requests failed` line instead of silently deflating throughput.
- Only `benchmark/hicache/bench_warm_cache.py` is changed.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — this is a benchmark client; it does not touch the model forward/output path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A for kernel/inference speed. The fix is validated by the identity `out_tps ≈ req/s * output_len` (exact because `ignore_eos` forces exactly `output_len` tokens per request): on the previously-contaminating config, 3/3 repeats now report `Total generated tokens == completed * 1024` and `out_tps == req/s * 1024`, versus ~1/3 contaminated before. Server-side `gen throughput` matches.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with `pre-commit` (ruff / ruff-format / isort).
- [ ] Add unit tests — N/A (benchmark script; happy to add a small SSE-parsing test if reviewers want one).
- [ ] Update documentation — N/A.
- [x] Provide benchmark verification (see above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style.

Hi @clintg6 (original author of this script) and hicache owners @xiezhq-hermann @huangtingwei9988 — gentle ping for review on this small **benchmark-only** fix. 🙏

**What it fixes:** `benchmark/hicache/bench_warm_cache.py` silently under-reports output-token throughput under high concurrency: some HTTP-200 requests are recorded as `success` with `output_len == 0` (token count was coupled to a non-empty `text` chunk, and any 200 was marked success), so `Total generated tokens` comes out an exact multiple of `output_len` short. The PR reads `meta_info.completion_tokens` on any chunk (monotonic max) and marks 0-token 200 responses as failed. No serving/runtime path is touched.

**Status:**
- `lint` and `gate` are green; the change is a single file and the branch is up-to-date with `main`.
- Commits are DCO signed-off.
- The remaining red checks are the fork-PR CI gate (`call-gate / pr-gate`) — the GPU/AMD/extra test matrices are `skipped` because they need a maintainer to authorize CI for an external fork. Could someone please trigger CI and take a look? Since it's benchmark-only I don't expect the GPU suites to be affected.

Happy to add a small SSE-parsing unit test if you'd like one. Thanks!
